svg.text: RECURRENT LAYER: ONE POSITION PER STEP
SELF-ATTENTION: ALL POSITIONS IN ONE STEP
done; the recurrent side is still going

a.data-tip: A recurrent model generates a sequence of hidden states, where the state at position t is a function of the state at t-1 and the input at t.
This state cannot be computed until h_1 exists. The dependency is on the previous step, not on the previous layer.
Because the chain is serial, the only parallelism left is across examples, and memory constraints limit that batching as sequences get longer.
Factorisation tricks and conditional computation have improved the constant factor, but the paper notes the fundamental constraint of sequential computation remains.
The last state is n steps away from the first, which is also why the maximum path length of a recurrent layer is O(n).

svg.text: h_t needs h_(t-1) first: n positions cost n steps, one after another

a.data-tip: Self-attention plus the position-wise feed-forward network process every position of the sequence in the same step, so the only serial dimension left is depth.
Every output position is a weighted sum over all input positions, so it depends on the whole sequence but on no other output.
No output waits for another output, so the whole row is one matrix multiply on the GPU.
Serialisation moves from the sequence axis to the depth axis: N = 6 layers, not n positions.
Order is not implied by the computation at all, which is exactly why positional encodings have to be added at the bottom of the stack.
The last position is one hop from the first, which is the O(1) maximum path length of Table 1.

svg.text: every z reads every x in one sub-layer; no z waits for another z

a.data-tip: The introduction names this as the fundamental constraint: aligning positions to steps in computation time precludes parallelization within training examples.
a.text: The paper: this inherently sequential nature precludes
parallelization within training examples, which becomes

a.data-tip: Table 1 gives a self-attention layer a constant number of sequentially executed operations, against O(n) for a recurrent layer.
a.text: In training, and always in the encoder, every position is
computed in the same step: long sentences add no sequential
steps. At inference the decoder still writes one token per step.

a.data-tip: Self-attention buys parallelism and short paths, and pays for them with a cost that is quadratic in the sequence length. The paper argues that is the right side of the trade for sentence-length inputs.
a.text: The trade the paper is making
Win: a new state of the art in translation quality after training for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.
Cost per layer (Table 1): self-attention scores all n x n pairs, each a d-wide dot product: O(n^2 . d). A recurrent layer
runs n steps, each a d x d matrix times a vector: O(n . d^2). Here d is the model width d_model = 512, not the 64-wide d_k.
So attention is the cheaper layer while sentence length n stays below 512; the paper says this is "most often" so, but quotes no lengths.
